evidence.summary: PIM systems are positioned as central sources of truth for collecting, managing, enriching, and distributing product information; benefits include reduced manual work, accuracy, consistency, and faster time-to-market.
evidence.confidence_effect: supports market need for centralized product/catalog management
evidence.limitations: General PIM source; does not validate Source BlendR-specific scraping, AI-provider agnosticism, or willingness to pay.

evidence.summary: Plytix positions PIM as a central product database with import options, validation, bulk editing, product data transformation, catalogs, AI product-description generation, and DAM support.
evidence.confidence_effect: supports competitive category and validates product-data management pain; shows AI exists in competing PIMs but often as product-copy assistance rather than provider-agnostic ingestion.
evidence.limitations: General PIM competitor source; product-centric and not focused on vendor website/PDF discovery staging.

evidence.summary: commonsku targets promotional products distributors with connected workflow, product search, presentations, portals, shops, CRM, suppliers, reports/analytics, integrations, and customer claims of operational time savings.
evidence.confidence_effect: supports existence of promo-distributor workflow market and validates adjacent demand for supplier/product workflow software.
evidence.limitations: Competitor positioning only; does not validate Source BlendR differentiation or pricing.

evidence.summary: Playwright supports navigation, clicking with auto-waiting, waiting for URL/load state, managing multiple pages and browser contexts, and capturing new pages/popups.
evidence.confidence_effect: supports feasibility of JS-rendered navigation and category traversal; does not guarantee reliability across arbitrary vendor sites.
evidence.limitations: Capability evidence only; no representative vendor-site test run was performed.

evidence.summary: Locks discovery-before-import, user-owned catalog, manual entry, PDF parity, background processing, AI-provider agnosticism, and Universal Catalog Items.
evidence.confidence_effect: supports product intent but not external validation.
evidence.limitations: Internal product artifact; not market evidence.

evidence.summary: Defines AI as an implementation detail behind adapters, provider registry, capability router, ingestion engine, and deterministic validation.
evidence.confidence_effect: supports architecture intent but not external user demand.

evidence.summary: Defines category-first strategy, lazy scraping, parallel category jobs, cached category trees, AI classification, and normalization.
evidence.confidence_effect: supports intended technical approach but not real-world reliability.
evidence.limitations: Internal architecture artifact; no executed test evidence.

stage_decision_brief.recommended_direction: Proceed to Stage 3 architecture with explicit architecture guidance and carried risks. Market and technical validation support the product direction at medium confidence, while willingness-to-pay, legal scraping posture, and real vendor-site reliability remain open validation items.
alternatives_considered: Proceed directly to architecture with open risks carried forward
Revise product assumptions around scraping and AI-provider agnosticism
Block progression until vendor-site testing and customer interviews are complete
key_decisions: PIM/catalog market problem is evidence-backed by Akeneo and Plytix PIM sources
Promo-distributor workflow market exists, supported by commonsku positioning and customer proof
Source BlendR remains differentiated by discovery-before-import, vendor-source ingestion, universal catalog items, and AI-provider agnosticism
Architecture may proceed if Stage 3 treats Playwright reliability, tenant isolation, validation engine, AI adapter contracts, and queue strategy as first-class decisions
downstream_impact: Stage 3 must design the scraping queue, retry, and observability model around unproven vendor-site variability
Stage 3 must isolate AI providers behind stable adapters and capability routing
Stage 3 must enforce deterministic validation before catalog writes
Stage 3 must include multi-tenant data and credential isolation as security-critical architecture
stage_decision_brief.approved_decision: Proceed to architecture with carried risks accepted

risk_registry.risk: Vendor-site scraping reliability remains unproven across representative websites.
risk_registry.mitigation: Stage 3 designs resilient crawler/queue; Stage 6 runs representative vendor-site tests.

risk_registry.risk: Multi-tenant isolation and AI credential isolation are security-critical.
risk_registry.mitigation: Stage 3 defines tenant boundaries, storage isolation, and credential handling; Stage 6 security tests.

risk_registry.risk: Willingness to pay is not directly validated.
risk_registry.mitigation: Run customer interviews and pricing tests before launch.
Stage 3 includes robots/ToS policy and manual opt-in controls; legal review before launch.

risk_registry.risk: Long-running background jobs can silently stall without observability.
risk_registry.mitigation: Stage 3 defines job status, retry/resume, idempotency, and operational telemetry.

validated_risks.rationale: Feasible primitives exist; real-site reliability untested.
PIM/category demand exists, but Source BlendR-specific willingness-to-pay is untested.

contradictions.description: PIM evidence validates centralized catalog pain but not AI-provider agnosticism as a buyer priority.
contradictions.impact: Differentiation may be weaker than assumed.

contradictions.description: PIM evidence is product-centric while Source BlendR includes services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, and installation.
contradictions.impact: Universal schema may need extension model.
contradictions.resolution_path: Stage 3 architecture should use base item with type-specific attributes.

critical_unknowns.unknown: Actual Playwright success rate on representative vendor websites.
critical_unknowns.next_action: Stage 6 test suite with target vendor sample.

critical_unknowns.unknown: Willingness to pay and buyer budget owner.
critical_unknowns.next_action: Run customer interviews and pricing tests.

critical_unknowns.unknown: Legal/ToS posture for scraping vendor websites.
critical_unknowns.next_action: Stage 3 policy and Stage 7 legal launch review.
